label: Invariant Geometry
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 51 through 70 and asks which geometric structures on a statistical manifold are natural rather than arbitrary. Demanding invariance under reparametrization and under sufficient statistics singles out the Fisher metric and a one-parameter family of connections.

label: Invariance and Sufficiency
notes: A meaningful geometry should not change when data are summarized by a sufficient statistic or relabeled by an invertible map. This requirement of invariance under Markov morphisms is the guiding principle that restricts which metrics and connections deserve to be called canonical.

label: Chentsov's Theorem
notes: Chentsov's theorem states that, up to a constant scale, the Fisher information metric is the only Riemannian metric invariant under sufficient statistics. This remarkable uniqueness result explains why the Fisher metric occupies the central place it does throughout statistics and information geometry.

label: The Alpha-Connections
notes: Beyond the metric, invariance permits a one-parameter family of affine connections indexed by a real number alpha. The values plus one and minus one give the exponential and mixture connections, while alpha equal to zero recovers the self-dual Levi-Civita connection of the Fisher metric.

label: f-Divergences
notes: An f-divergence is built from a convex function applied to the ratio of two densities, and every such divergence is invariant under sufficient statistics. The Kullback-Leibler, Hellinger, and chi-squared divergences are members, each inducing the same invariant Fisher metric to second order.

label: Invariant Divergence
notes: The alpha-divergences form the invariant family that interpolates between the exponential and mixture sides. Their geometry reproduces the Fisher metric and the alpha-connections, closing the circle: invariant divergences, invariant metric, and invariant connections all arise from the same principle.
